published_prior_art.cite: CorreaTianBareinboim2019Selection: IDSB already gives a sound recursion for the identical selected-conditional-plus-margin input.
KivvaMokhtarianEtesamiKiyavash2022GID supplies related positive-law perturbation witnesses; the normalized selected-law projective rows are a targeted extension.
CorreaTianBareinboim2019Selection leaves positive two-law cases outside IDSB unresolved; ShpitserPearl2006JointID supplies only one-law hedge witnesses.
DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds provides response-function polynomial machinery, but not this exhaustive selected-conditional-plus-margin equivalence census.
CorreaTianBareinboim2019Selection proves IDSB sound, while explicitly leaving whether further positive cases exist unresolved.
TikkaHyttinenKarvanen2021DoSearch is sound for arbitrary input distributions and proves negative-answer completeness only for its specified already-complete Table 1 rows.
vanDerVaart1998 supplies the finite-dimensional delta-method result; this is its direct two-independent-multinomial specialization.
Standard fixed-dimensional multinomial plug-in consistency plus Bonferroni inversion gives this result on a positive compact class.

novelty_flags.label: related_work; novelty_justification; thm:dosearch-scope-separation
novelty_flags.one_line: The core attributes Rows 1--4 and 6 failure-completeness to do-search Theorem 2, but the JSS paper labels Theorem 2 as soundness and termination; the stated negative-answer result is Theorem 3.

soundness_flags.label: def:extid-state-machine and thm:extid-sound-termination
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed finite universe includes unrestricted probability-calculus combinations and is ordered by derivation length without a grammar bound or semantic quotient, so neither finiteness of mathscr U nor the stated termination bound is defined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:conditional-extid-completeness
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Universal completeness is conditional on resolving the margin-anchored hedge question for every terminal failure and on a collision-free three-node audit.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline completeness claim is only: EXT-ID is complete for the exact two-law problem after those two stated research gates are discharged.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2747--2750, Definition 4, Algorithm 3, Theorem 4, and discussion immediately before Theorem 5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 4 uses P(V|S=1) together with P(T0); Algorithm 3 takes those inputs; Theorem 4 states IDSB is sound; the paper says it remains unclear whether positive recoverable cases exist where IDSB returns FAIL.
Theorem 2 states that do-search terminates and is sound. Theorem 3, not Theorem 2, states that an NA output proves nonidentifiability in Table 1 Rows 1--4 and 6.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1023, Definition 1; pp. 1025--1026, Theorem 1 and the gID discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines positivity through strictly positive observed cells and gives a sound-and-complete general-identifiability algorithm; it does not establish the selected-conditional-plus-external-margin projective fiber.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 6 and Corollaries 2--3 on the final pages
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For a full observational distribution, ID is complete and its failure yields the hedge criterion for nonidentifiability.
The paper gives a sound systematic-selection identification algorithm and explicitly conjectures that the algorithm is also complete.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the candidate universe with a bounded canonical grammar for kernels and arithmetic operations, or prove a finite semantic normal-form quotient; then state the resulting explicit complexity or termination bound.
Correct every do-search theorem-number citation to Theorem 3 for failure completeness, while retaining Theorem 2 only for soundness and termination.
Before universal work, exhibit a nontrivial three-node selected-law-plus-margin terminal failure and its fully interior projective witness, then make the exact audit test that example first.

recommended_next_step: Revise the finite-state-machine definition and do-search attribution, then continue at Stage 0 with the accepted conditional-completeness scope.
